FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by-the Made-up Textiles (Other Than Ready-made Garments) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. The term `ground sheet' is used for a rectangular waterproof sheet made from rubber proofed light weight double texture fabric hemmed and fitted with eyelets and washers on its four sides. For the purpose of deciding-whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard

TEXTILES - GROUND SHEETS ( LIGHT WEIGHT ) - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE This specification covers the requirements of light weight ground sheet made from light weight double-texture rubberized waterproof fabric. 2 REFERENCES Indian Standards listed at Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 MATERIALS 3.1 Basic fabric for ground sheets shall be cotton calico OG (see IS 1544 : 1973) and shade of rubber proofed fabric shall also be OG colour to match with the shade of base fabric. 3.2 The body of ground sheets shall be manufactured from double-texture rubberized water proof fabric conforming to the following requirements when tested in accordance with IS 6110 : 1983: d) Adhesion strength i) Original Average 30 N but not less than 20 N in any of two directions Not less than 75 percent of the original load 4OO-e20

IS 14351: 1996 4 MANUFACTURE The sheet shall be made from one rectangular piece of light weight double-texture rubberized waterproof fabric. The hem shall be formed on the four sides of this piece as shown in Fig. 1. Washers cut from rubber proofed light weight double texture fabric shall be inserted in position within the fold of the hem, except at corners, to take in the eyelets. The hem and the washer shall be securely fixed by means of rubber solution. In addition,the hem shall be machine stitched with spun polyester sewing thread, along the inner edge, with a single row of stitching. The stitching shall consist of not less than 30 stitches per decimetre. The eyelets shall be free from manufacturing defects and shall be properly clenched to a smooth finish. One eyelet shall be fured at each corner and the remaining eyelets shall be spaced equally between the corner eyelets seven on each side and two at each end as shown in Fig. 1. 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Workmanship and Finish Ground sheets shall be flexible and free from cuts, objectionable weaving flaws such as broken or missing ends or picks and knots ittbasic fabric and from creases, wrinkles, oil and other stains, pinholes, thin places, joints and other manufacturing defects in the double texture fabric. 5.2 Dimensions and Mass 5.2.1 The sheets shall conform to the dimensions and other details as shown in Fig. 1. A tolerance of -c 10 mm is permissible in the length and the width of ground sheets. 5.2.2 The mass of ground sheets, when determined after conditioning the sample for 48 hours in an atmosphere of 65 -+ 2 percent relative humidity and temperature of 27 +- 2�C shall not be more than 1.0 kg. 6 MARKING 6.1 Each ground sheet shall be legibly and indelibly marked at one of the corners on the underside with the following information: i) Brief nomenclature, ii) Manufacturer's name/initials or recognized trade-mark, and iii) Month and year of manufacture. 6.1.1 BIS Certification Marking
The ground sheets may also be marked with the

6.1.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau uf Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6.2 Each bale containing ground sheets shall also be legibly marked by stencil with indelible marking ink/paint as under : Name/initials or recognized trade-mark -of the supplier, ii) Month and year of packaging, iii) Gross mass of bale in kg, iv) Quantity packed in the bale, v) Lot and serial number of bale, and vi) Any other marking required by the buyer.

9

7 PACKAGING 7.1 Each ground sheet shall be dusted with french chalk (see IS 380 : 1978) for preservation and five such ground sheets placed one over the other in a slightly staggered position shall be rolled to form a roll and tied neatly and securely with 3 ply jute twine (see IS 1912 : 1984) or equivalent string at appropriate places over the roll to form a unit pack. A suitable number of such unit packs shall be wrapped with an inner layer of polyethylene film (see IS 2508 : 1984) or waxed paper (see IS 3962 : 1%7)/inner layer of kraft paper (see IS 1397 : 1990) with an outer layer of bitumen laminated waterproof packing paper (see IS 1398 : 1982) may be used to form a bundle. 7.2 Each bundle then shall be wrapped with a layer of heavy tee jute cloth (see IS 3751: 1993) or double layer of 229 g/m2 hessian [see IS 2818(Part 2) : 19711 to form a compact bale of rectangular shape as far as possible. Alternatively suitable number of unit packs may be wrapped with an inner and an outer layer of laminated hessian cloth to form the bale. The bale shallnot be press packed. 7.3 The overlapping of inner wrapping shall be atleast 10 cm so as to ensure full protection to content of the bale. The overlapping of outer layer of hessian cloth shall be such that it can be properly and securely sewn around the bale. 7.4 The bale shall be stitched with double 3 ply jute twine with minimum 6 stitches per decimetre taking care not to pierce the contents of the bale during stitching. Sufficient hessian cloth shall be pulled out of each corner to form `ears' of about 15 cm in length to facilitate easy handling during transit. 2

Standard Mark.

IS 14351: 1996 7.5 Wooden slats approximately 7 cm wide and 1 cm thick and free from rot or other harmful fungal or insect attack or alternatively bamboo strips duly preserved shall be placed lengthwise along the edges of bale and finally bound with atleast 3 bands of polypropylene strapping of 12 mm width along the length of bale. The bale shall not be press packed. 7.6 The mass of bale shall not exceed 40 kg. 8 SAMPLING 8.1 Lot The quantity of ground sheets delivered to a buyer against a despatch note shall constitute a lot. 8.2 The conformity of the lot to the requirements of the standard shall be determined on the basis of tests carried out on the sample selected from it. BIS is a statutory institution established under the Burenc~ of Indian Stmf~rds Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard alsng with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
